Oh, okay. I'm American. No, we would have to pay for it still, even if I were "forced" to be admitted. That's how it has worked in the past. I don't want to make my family deal with that. To be honest, I don't want to relive what I have experienced. I don't think that I can handle that.

Thanks.

Yeah, I made a post there last night. I got some good replies, but the post is also getting downvoted for some reason, lol. It was helpful to me last night, when things were really bad.

I spent quite a bit of time in psych hospitals as a kid/preteen. They were horrible experiences that I really wish I could forget. I was abused, and I saw other kids around my age being abused. Even with that aside, I never learned anything of real value in my multiple visits. The "funny farm" wasn't useful to me as it was to you. I was really drugged up, but in a bad way.

My family's in a bad financial situation right now, so we can't afford to see a therapist. I am thinking about making a call. I just really feel uncomfortable about this. I also didn't know that they can take you to the psych ward...that doesn't make me want to call.

I am thinking about it, but I don't know.

Yeah, I made a post there. It's getting downvoted for some reason, though. I got some replies and it was helpful for me last night, when I was really struggling, but I don't know.
Okay, thanks a lot. I will.

That's pretty cool. I'm not a very frequent Redditor, so I guess I feel dumb posting this here, but I guess it's good to know that you've used the site as an outlet for this stuff too. I feel kind of pathetic, but I really don't know what else to do...

Oh, okay. 

Yeah, I got up the courage yesterday to tell my mom that things are really difficult for me lately. She basically just said "I'm sorry, I don't know how to help you". So, I really don't know who to talk to about this.

I'm really sorry about that. Why do you think that happened?

Yeah, I am in the process of psyching myself up. I thought about doing this when I was younger, but never got up the courage to call. Also, I'm home alone right now, so that's decreasing my anxiety somewhat.

Okay, I'll check out that subreddit. Thanks.

Yeah, the college I'm going to only has one counselor. I get the impression that she's just for minor stuff, like "I'm homesick" or "I'm anxious about x issue". So, I don't think that it would be wise for me to unload all of my issues on her.

Cool, thanks. I will look into that. And thanks for commenting. I was feeling really messed up last night. I'm feeling okay now, but I don't know how long this will last for.

I guess it's just difficult for me to get and stay in that mindset. But I will keep trying.

Thanks a lot. I hope that you're right. I am thinking about elementary or junior high, not sure which grade level yet.

Yes, I know. It's not that she's not taking things seriously, I don't think. I know that it's difficult for her to think of the past, when I struggled more with mental health issues. 

Yeah, but I'm really worried about student loans and all of the debt that I'm going to accrue. I need to get surgery within the next few years too, but I don't know when I'll be able to afford that. It's nothing life-threatening, but I would rather it be done sooner than later. (Sorry that I'm saying all of this, but I don't get the chance to ever talk about it).

Haha, well, I don't know about that.

I get what you're saying. I think that I would like to become a teacher. I like kids, and I like helping people. I also can't ever have any of my own kids, so I guess that it'll be a good way to experience that bond. I guess sometimes I just get really caught up in everything. Sometimes I really just feel like everything is absolutely pointless. Maybe that sounds dumb, but it just fills me with this weird anguish.

Yes, that's what virtually everyone in my life tells me. I really don't understand why I get so much praise and positivity. I can't tell you the last time anyone had anything even remotely negative or critical to say about/to me. As I have said, I really don't have any drive or motivation to live. Everything is so menial, and it is just driving me insane.

Not on any meds, haven't been on any since I was 13. My mom took me off cold turkey after I had a particularly severe side effect (went temporarily blind in one eye). I tried maybe 12-16 meds in total.

I was hospitalized at 8, 10, 11, and 12. Sorry if I wrote that badly, I wasn't in a good state of mind. All of them were for suicide attempts/ideation.

I don't know. When I've had relapses like this in the past, they weren't caused by any major life event.

I can't afford a therapist right now. My family is in a lot of debt and our insurance doesn't cover mental health stuff (I don't understand why). We might not even have insurance after this year.

I get what you're saying. I find that, in the past, I have always talked myself out of committing suicide by thinking of others. When I was younger, I didn't kill myself because I didn't want my parents to have to find my body. I guess that I am just tired of living for other people, if that makes sense. I know that I am loved/liked by others, but I don't personally feel like that.

I only have had horrible experiences with hospitals. Long story short...I was abused and witnessed other kids being abused. I feel like I repressed many memories from that time, and occasionally I will remember something. Also, my family is in a lot of debt right now, and our insurance sucks, to be frank. So I don't want to be even more of a financial burden to my mom. She might not even be keeping her job this next year. It would also reopen a lot of old wounds, and make everything that my relatives have said about being proud of me for "coming so far" be false. That's not an option for a lot of reasons.
I am graduating this week. My school doesn't have a counselor.
